objects.original: Convex-class solver, strongly convex target, minimizer and iterated outputs.
objects.reconstructed: A supplied point/cost map A, fixed f and z, actual recursively defined points and summed natural costs.
objects.evidence: The packet module implements each call as A y r delta and propagates its returned point and cost; no radius invariant or final answer is substituted for execution. The map has no oracle restriction.

domains.original: Euclidean objective with smoothness parameter beta and positive strong-convexity modulus.
domains.reconstructed: A complete real inner-product space with C1, alpha-strongly convex f on all E; beta occurs only in the cost contract.
domains.evidence: Euclidean spaces specialize the stated Hilbert domain. The proof needs differentiability for the gradient lower bound; Lipschitz-gradient smoothness is not inferred from beta. This is a disclosed generalization of the finite composition component, not equivalence of function classes.

quantifiers.original: A single solver works over the convex smooth class; restart transforms it to a class-uniform algorithm.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For each fixed f and minimizer z, every A and phi satisfying the uniform-in-y,r,delta contract satisfy the displayed conclusions.
quantifiers.evidence: All calls use the same f and z. The theorem does not quantify over a class-uniform first-order implementation. Every natural N satisfying alpha*(R/2^N)^2<=epsilon is allowed, including N=0.

assumptions.original: Radius-certified base optimization guarantee, strongly convex smooth objective and attained minimizer.
assumptions.reconstructed: Positive alpha,beta,R,epsilon; supplied global minimizer; initial upper-radius bound; C1 strong convexity; explicit solver output and cost contract.
assumptions.evidence: The opening Section 4.1 convention admits an upper radius certificate. At every stage the passed radius equals the scheduled radius; the final radius equals sqrt(epsilon/alpha). Therefore evaluating phi at 8*kappa and kappa needs no monotonicity. Positive parameters give valid calls. The algebraic horizon premise supplies exactly the radius needed for the final call.

conclusion.original: Radius halving and final accuracy support the full logarithmic first-order-query reduction.
conclusion.reconstructed: Actual radius and final error, with certified finite cumulative cost. For any adequate N, c_N<=N*phi(8*kappa) and C<=N*phi(8*kappa)+phi(kappa).
conclusion.evidence: Each displayed conjunction agrees with the elaborated Lean statement and blind reconstruction. The theorem does not select N or state a logarithmic estimate. No first-order-query theorem follows without realizing the certified solver contract in the oracle/class model.

scopes.original: An algorithmic reduction, whose proof contains finite call composition and asymptotic counting.
scopes.evidence: Binding supports restart-radius, finite-accuracy-cost only. The updated obligation asymptotic-oracle-reduction is explicitly not closed. The finite parent gains no new logarithmic coverage merely because that obligation appears in the common source context.

constant_dependencies.original: Halving follows from alpha/2 quadratic growth with tolerance alpha*r^2/8; per-call budget uses kappa=beta/alpha.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Exactly the same factors 1/2, 1/8 and 8*kappa, with a separate phi(kappa) final term. The stage multiplier is the supplied N and the last cost is included even when N=0.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The authored algebra matches the packet proof. Quadratic growth bounds the next squared distance by r_k^2/4; positivity gives halving. Exact cancellation in each passed radius/tolerance ratio avoids a hidden comparison of different phi arguments.

deltas.description: Hilbert/C1 finite-component generalization; beta is a budget parameter in the formal theorem.
deltas.evidence: Current module assumptions and lesson describe the actual domain. Euclidean beta-smooth objectives fit the intended application, but that class-to-contract adapter is outside this declaration.

deltas.description: Full source class-uniform first-order solver realization remains uncovered.
deltas.evidence: A is an unconstrained point/cost map apart from hA for fixed f,z. Publication keeps asymptotic-oracle-reduction separate and explicitly not closed.

deltas.description: Finite radius/accuracy/cost component accepted; adequate horizon remains an input.
deltas.evidence: The binding supports only restart-radius and finite-accuracy-cost; the shared new logarithmic obligation does not alter the finite theorem statement or lesson.
